correctness.rationale: For each vertex select an ordered two-vector; edge bracket coefficients are oriented determinants. Fixing the exact nonzero column set U forces W(B)⊆U. On each induced tree every root has q²−1 nonzero choices and each zero/nonzero labelled edge has exactly q−1/q choices for the child; there are no cycle compatibility conditions. Multiply independent components and q^(2m) free central coordinates, then sum over U. Checks were executed on all 277 small prescribed targets over F2,F3,F4 and normalization, but all-q validity rests on the explicit proof.

originality.rationale: The primary graphical Lie-algebra source defines the objects and studies automorphisms. Rossmann fully treats graphical group conjugacy and centralizer distributions but not pointwise prescribed nonzero-bracket fibers. The induced-component polynomial covers the zero-target case (credited as prior), not the nonzero prescribed target support law. Prior finite quiver associative commutator fibers use another bilinear map and cannot imply the graph Lie determinant count as stated. Targeted published-finding corpus and publication searches found no dominating same-object theorem; historical equivalents remain a genuine residual risk.

value.rationale: The bracket-fiber distribution is a natural full two-variable commutator word-map invariant, refining centralizer counts and commuting probability. It is determined for arbitrary forests and all finite fields, proves surjectivity onto the commutator subspace, and exposes nontrivial positional dependence even among one-edge-supported targets on the same path. The result is not merely a normalization, existing zero-target polynomial restatement or arbitrary isolated finite enumeration.
